# New-ZbxModule

## SYNOPSIS

Creates a frontend module.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxModule [-ModuleIdentifier <string>] [-RelativePath <string>] [-Status <ZabbixModuleStatus>] [-Config <JsonElement>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A frontend module adds widgets or pages to the Zabbix frontend; it is listed once its files are in the frontend's modules folder, and runs once enabled. The New-ZbxModule cmdlet sends module.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new frontend module back with module.get and writes it. The server requires -ModuleIdentifier and -RelativePath; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create a frontend module

```powershell
New-ZbxModule -ModuleIdentifier 'inventory-report' -RelativePath 'modules/inventory-report' -Status Enabled
```

Creates a frontend module. The command writes the new frontend module, read back from the server.

- `string`: Bound to -ModuleIdentifier (ByPropertyName), -RelativePath (ByPropertyName). Text.
- `ZabbixModuleStatus`: Bound to -Status (ByPropertyName). The module status values: MODULE_STATUS_* in defines.inc.php.
